content.tldr: A follower broker is evicted from the ISR when it fails to send fetch requests to the leader within the configured `replica.lag.time.max.ms` window due to network, crash, or GC pauses.
content.simple_explanation: The leader partition continuously monitors the replication progress of its followers. If a follower crashes, suffers a long JVM stop-the-world garbage collection pause, experiences network partition, or has insufficient I/O bandwidth to keep pace with incoming writes, the time elapsed since its last caught-up fetch request exceeds `replica.lag.time.max.ms`. The leader immediately updates cluster metadata to drop that follower from the active ISR list.
content.real_world_example: A satellite relay chain: if one ground station stops sending ping acknowledgments for more than 30 seconds, the central coordinator drops that station from the active broadcast routing table.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Frequent ISR churn (brokers constantly dropping out and rejoining) causes significant Controller metadata updates and performance stutter. This typically indicates undersized broker disk I/O or undersized network bandwidth.
